title: The ecosystem communications infrastructure is mandated with a quarterly budget of zero
content:
A.2.7.1.3 states in full: "The ecosystem communication infrastructure budget is 0 USDS per quarter."

That sits against a substantial standing obligation. A.2.7.1.1 tasks the Core Facilitator "with maintaining an ecosystem-wide communications infrastructure," A.2.7.1.1.1 requires it to include a Forum, and A.2.7.1.1.2 requires a chatroom. On top of hosting, the Article layers real operational work: moderating four channels, maintaining the Authorized Forum Accounts registry, drafting public ban notices, and preparing unbanning polls.

A zero line item does not mean the work is unfunded — it means it is funded somewhere else, most plausibly inside the Core Facilitator's own allocation from the Core Council, and that the ecosystem is not tracking its cost separately. A.2.7.1.1.2 hints at how the bill is kept near zero: "As an initial bootstrapping measure, the Core Facilitator can use Discord," a free third-party platform.

The consequence worth noting is dependency rather than expense. Governance discussion, the settlement threads where Initial and Final Calculations are posted, dispute decisions, and the unbanning process all run on infrastructure with no dedicated resourcing and, in the chatroom case, on a platform the ecosystem does not control. A.2.7.1.2.2 also disperses moderation across the Core Facilitator and two Ecosystem Actors for X and Reddit, none of it funded by this line.

The forum in particular is load-bearing for processes the Atlas treats as binding, which makes a zero budget a mismatch between how critical the infrastructure is and how it is accounted for.
description: The Core Facilitator must maintain a forum and chatroom for the whole ecosystem, yet A.2.7.1.3 sets the communications infrastructure budget at 0 USDS per quarter.
